newsitem.title: USA: U.S. arrests 34 in international heroin ring bust.
newsitem.headline: U.S. arrests 34 in international heroin ring bust.

text.p: The Clinton administration announced on Friday the arrests of 34 suspects in three nations, smashing an alleged drug ring run mainly by Nigerian women that smuggled Asian heroin into the United States.

President Bill Clinton, who has been attacked by Republican rival Bob Dole as being soft on drugs, immediately hailed the drug bust. "The break-up of this drug network marks anotheone in our effort to cripple major international drug trafficking cartels," Clinton said in a statement.
Justice Department spokesman Bert Brandenburg denied any political motivation in the timing of the case, which came just a few weeks before the Nov. 5 presidential election.
"Absolutely not," he said, adding that the White House learned about it only when the arrests were announced.

Attorney General Janet Reno said more than 100 federal and local law enforcement officers on Friday morning broke up the alleged international heroin-smuggling ring. "They arrested 34 of its members at five locations around the world, including Bangkok, Pakistan, New York, Chicago and Detroit," she told a news conference.

The year-long operation code-named "Global Sea" involved what Reno called an "unprecedented display of cooperation" by law enforcement officials in Thailand, France and Great Britain "to dismantle an international drug ring run predominantly by Nigerian women."
She added: "This drug ring allegedly stretched from the opium fields of Southeast Asia to the streets of America."
U.S. officials said they seized more than 120 pounds (55 kg) of heroin with an estimated total retail value exceeding $26 million. In all, 44 people have been charged in the case.

Drug Enforcement Administration chief Thomas Constantine said the case marked the first time so many women had been involved in a drug smuggling ring, rising to a leadership position while also serving as couriers.
"It also demonstrates that Nigerian criminal organisations are no longer just couriers but have developed into major heroin traffickers in their own right," he said.

U.S. officials said the heroin originated in Thailand and Cambodia. Under one route it was shipped directly to Boston, while the other route involved transporting it through Paris or Amsterdam to Guatemala, into Mexico and then to Chicago for distribution throughout the Midwest.

The case started in Boston with a U.S. Customs Service agent and in Milwaukee when two DEA agents made a small drug buy. Officials said agents, using court-authorised wiretaps that intercepted more than 25,000 telephone calls, were able to penetrate the drug ring.

Among the key figures charged were Anthony Smith, who was arrested in Bangkok; Musiliu Balogun, who remains at large; and Jumoke Kafayat Majekodunmi, owner of a women's clothing boutique in Chicago. Also charged were two Boston policemen who served as drug couriers.
